# Two entries that print in one place and file under two keys

The index tool the LaTeX back-end writes for stores three levels. An entry
written deeper is folded into its third level rather than dropped, so two
entries whose level paths differ before the fold can be identical after it.
Sort keys are declared against the paths an author wrote, which the fold does
not change, so each of the two keeps a key of its own — and the index tool,
reading two different keys, files the one printed entry twice and prints it
twice, in two places, identically.

Every pair below is that collision, so this fixture is a document of mistakes
rather than one to copy. Its twin, `sortkey-clamp-twin.qmd`, writes the same
entries with one shared key per pair, which is the same document without the
mistake.

The HTML back-end applies no such ceiling — the fold is the index tool's
limit, not an index's — so there the four entries below stay four, at the
level paths they were written with.

## One side folded, the other written folded

Four levels against three whose third level spells the folded form. `Zed` is
written for the four-level entry's third level and `Ada` for the other's, so
the two file apart although both print at `alpha!beta!gamma, delta`:

[Delta]{.index entry="alpha!beta!gamma!delta" sort="alpha!beta!Zed"} and
[Gamma, delta]{.index entry="alpha!beta!gamma, delta" sort="alpha!beta!Ada"}.

## Both sides folded

Five levels against four. Neither entry is written at the printed depth this
time — the fold builds the same third level out of two different tails — and
`Wye` and `Vee` file the result two ways:

[Pi]{.index entry="mu!nu!xi!omicron!pi" sort="mu!nu!Wye"} and
[Omicron, pi]{.index entry="mu!nu!xi, omicron!pi" sort="mu!nu!Vee"}.
